title: PUC2-Sub Case 2d: CACAO Playbook Authoring Training (Malicious IP Block)
description: A hands-on training for the CyberRangeCZ Platform that follows the 16-step PUC2 Sub Case 2d UML sequence. The Student authors a CACAO 2.0 playbook in NG-SOAR (KMS) to block a malicious source IP on the Lab Target Service host firewall (nftables input), gets it validated by the NG-SOAR CACAO Validator, the NG-SOAR Operator executes it, NG-SOAR verifies the block from the malicious IP and returns the evidence, and the Cyber Range compiles the results for Evaluation/Reporting, which returns the training summary. Designed for the lm8-1d sandbox (single flat network, host-based enforcement on lab-target).
prerequisites: Basic Linux command line (cat, ls, curl, grep, ssh, a text editor).
Basic understanding of host firewalls and IP addressing.
No prior CACAO knowledge required - it is taught in the training.
outcomes: Explain the purpose of CACAO 2.0 playbooks and the role of NG-SOAR (KMS + CACAO Validator/Executor).
Author a valid CACAO block-IP playbook from the templates provided by the Cyber Range.
Interpret NG-SOAR validation errors, correct and resubmit a playbook until it is approved.
Understand the separation of duties: the Student authors, the NG-SOAR Operator executes.
Verify a host-firewall (nftables input) source-IP block from the execution evidence.
Read the training summary compiled by the Cyber Range and returned by Evaluation/Reporting.

levels.title: 1. Welcome - PUC2 Sub Case 2d
levels.content:
# CACAO Playbook Authoring Training - Malicious IP Block

The **NG-SOC Operator** (scenario initiator) has launched this exercise on the
**Hands-on Educational Platform (Cyber Range)**. A test host with a **malicious
IP** is probing the **Lab Target Service**.

You play the **Student (Trainee)**: you will author a **CACAO 2.0** playbook in
**NG-SOAR** that blocks the malicious source IP on the **target host firewall
(nftables `input` chain)**, get it validated, and review the evidence and the
final training summary. In the *Execution* phase you will temporarily switch
hats and act as the **NG-SOAR Operator**, the only role allowed to execute an
approved playbook.

The training follows the 16-step UML sequence in five phases:

| # | Levels | Phase | UML steps |
|:-:|--------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | 1-3 | Introduction and access | - |
| 2 | 4-8 | Scenario kickoff | 1-3 |
| 3 | 9-17 | CACAO playbook creation | 4-6 |
| 4 | 18-23 | Validation | 7-10 |
| 5 | 24-31 | Execution | 11-14 |
| 6 | 32-35 | Feedback | 15-16 |

**Tip:** the Chrome browser works best. If a submission misbehaves, log out and
back in.

levels.title: 2. Actors, components and hosts
levels.content:
# Who is who

| UML participant | In this sandbox |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| NG-SOC Operator (Scenario Initiator) | Your instructor: starts the training run on the platform (UML 1) |
| Student (Trainee) | **You**, working from the Cyber Range trainee console |
| NG-SOAR Operator | The only role allowed to execute approved playbooks (you will role-play it in levels 27-28) |
| Hands-on Educational Platform (Cyber Range) | CyberRangeCZ + the trainee console `student-ws` (brief, toolkit, `cacao-client`, `cr-compile`) |
| NG-SOAR (KMS + CACAO Validator/Executor) | `ng-soar` - API on port 9100, operator console `soar-operator` |
| Attacker (malicious test IP) | `attacker` |
| Lab Target Service (host firewall - nftables) | `lab-target` - HTTP/SSH service **and** enforcement point |
| Evaluation/Reporting | `evaluation-reporting` - API on port 9000 |

## Hosts (one flat network `10.10.0.0/16`)

| Host | IP | Role |
|------|----|------|
| student-ws | 10.10.30.20 | Cyber Range trainee console (you) |
| ng-soar | 10.10.30.10 | NG-SOAR: KMS + CACAO Validator/Executor |
| evaluation-reporting | 10.10.30.30 | Evaluation/Reporting |
| attacker | 10.10.10.10 | Malicious test IP |
| lab-target | 10.10.20.10 | Lab Target Service + host firewall (nftables `input`) |

## Student commands (`cacao-client`)
```sh
cacao-client create  ~/cacao/my_playbook.json   # UML 4  - create the playbook in NG-SOAR (KMS)
cacao-client submit  ~/cacao/my_playbook.json   # UML 6/9 - submit (or resubmit) for validation
cacao-client status  ~/cacao/my_playbook.json   # UML 10 - KMS status of your playbook
cacao-client report  ~/cacao/my_playbook.json   # UML 14 - execution logs, status, firewall evidence
cacao-client summary                            # UML 16 - training summary
```
The Student **cannot execute** playbooks - that is the NG-SOAR Operator's job.

levels.title: 3. Access the Cyber Range trainee console
levels.cloud_content:
Get into the sandbox from where you will do everything else. When connected,
submit the passkey **`start`**.

### Connect via the GUI console
1. In the topology view on the right, **right-click `student-ws`** and choose
   **Open console**.
2. Log in with the sandbox credentials provided by your instructor.

### Or connect via SSH
SSH makes copy-pasting commands easier. See the
[sandbox access documentation](https://docs.platform.cyberrange.cz/user-guide-advanced/sandboxes/sandbox-access/#user-access).

Then submit **`start`** to continue.
levels.local_content: This training is designed for the cloud sandbox on the CyberRangeCZ Platform.

levels.title: 4. Phase 1 - Scenario kickoff (UML 1-3)
levels.content:
# Scenario kickoff

- **UML 1** - The **NG-SOC Operator** initiates the CACAO playbook authoring
  exercise on the **Hands-on Educational Platform** (this training run).
- **UML 2** - The **Cyber Range** makes the **Attacker** generate suspicious
  traffic from a test IP against the **Lab Target Service** (probing `/admin`,
  `/.env` and port 22).
- **UML 3** - The **Cyber Range** hands you the **exercise brief**: *block the
  malicious IP on the target host firewall*.

In the next levels you will read the brief, identify the protected service and
recognise the malicious activity.

levels.title: 5. Read the exercise brief (UML 3)
levels.content:
The Cyber Range delivered the exercise brief to your console at
`~/cacao/EXERCISE_BRIEF.md`. Identify the **malicious source IP** you are asked
to block.

**Answer:** the malicious source IP.
levels.solution:
1. `cat ~/cacao/EXERCISE_BRIEF.md`.
2. Under *Scenario* it lists `Malicious source IP : ${ANSWER}`.
3. Submit **`${ANSWER}`**.

hints.title: Where is the brief?
hints.content: In your home directory under `~/cacao/`. Try `cat ~/cacao/EXERCISE_BRIEF.md`.

levels.title: 6. Identify the protected service (UML 2-3)
levels.content:
Open the service under attack and read the exact **page title** it serves.
The brief tells you it is at `http://10.10.20.10:80`.

**Answer:** the `<h1>` title shown on the landing page (exact text).
levels.solution:
1. `curl -s http://10.10.20.10/`. 2. The HTML contains `

Lab Target Service

`. 3. Submit **`Lab Target Service`** (exact casing).

hints.title: Reading a web page from the console
hints.content: Use `curl -s http://10.10.20.10/` and look at the `<h1>` heading.

levels.title: 7. Spot the suspicious traffic (UML 2)
levels.content:
The brief ships with the detection evidence of the suspicious traffic generated
by the malicious IP: `~/cacao/detected_traffic.log`.

**Answer:** the sensitive *dotfile* path the attacker keeps requesting.
levels.solution:
1. `cat ~/cacao/detected_traffic.log`.
2. The attacker loops `GET /admin`, `GET /.env` and a port-22 probe.
3. The secrets dotfile is **`/.env`**. Submit it.

hints.title: What are attackers usually after?
hints.content: Configuration/secret files. One of the probed paths is a well-known secrets dotfile.

levels.title: 8. Kickoff knowledge check

questions.text: Where will the malicious source IP be blocked?

choices.text: On the host firewall (nftables input chain) of the Lab Target Service
On a dedicated network firewall between two networks
The NG-SOC Operator, on the Hands-on Educational Platform

questions.text: What is the IP address of the protected Lab Target Service?

levels.instructions: A short test on the scenario kickoff phase.

levels.title: 9. Phase 2 - CACAO playbook creation (UML 4-6)
levels.content:
# CACAO playbooks

**CACAO 2.0** is a standard for **interoperable, machine-readable security
playbooks**: a JSON document describing a *workflow* of steps
(`start` -> `action` -> `end`) that automates an incident-response procedure.

In this phase:

- **UML 4** - you **create** the block-IP playbook **in NG-SOAR** (it is stored in
  the NG-SOAR **KMS** as a *draft*);
- **UML 5** - the **Cyber Range** gives you **templates, schema hints and the
  supported firewall commands** (already in `~/cacao/`);
- **UML 6** - you **submit** the playbook for validation (next phase).

levels.title: 10. Explore the toolkit (UML 5)
levels.content:
List the materials the Cyber Range provided in `~/cacao/` and identify the
**template file** you should start from.

**Answer:** the exact filename of the block-IP template.
levels.solution:
1. `ls ~/cacao/`.
2. You see `template_block_ip.json`, `schema_hints.md`,
   `supported_firewall_commands.md` and `sample_block_ip_playbook.json`.
3. Submit **`template_block_ip.json`**.

hints.title: Template vs sample
hints.content: The *template* is the skeleton you fill in; the *sample* is a full worked example.

levels.title: 11. Schema hints: spec_version (UML 5)
levels.content:
Read `~/cacao/schema_hints.md` and find the **exact value** required for the
`spec_version` field.

**Answer:** the spec_version value as it must appear in the JSON.
levels.solution:
1. `cat ~/cacao/schema_hints.md`.
2. `spec_version` must be **`cacao-2.0`**.
3. Submit **`cacao-2.0`**.

hints.title: Where are the field rules?
hints.content: See the *Required top-level fields* table in `schema_hints.md`.

levels.title: 12. Supported firewall commands: the chain (UML 5)
levels.content:
The block is enforced by the **host firewall (nftables)** of the Lab Target
Service. Read `~/cacao/supported_firewall_commands.md` and identify the
**chain** into which the drop rule is added.

**Answer:** the nftables chain name.
levels.solution:
1. `cat ~/cacao/supported_firewall_commands.md`.
2. The block command is `sudo nft add rule inet filter input ip saddr <IP> counter drop`.
3. The chain for packets destined to the host itself is **`input`**.

hints.title: Chains in nftables
hints.content: To drop packets arriving AT a host you use the chain hooked on host-bound (ingress-to-host) traffic.

levels.title: 13. Start from the template (UML 4)
levels.content:
Copy the template to your working playbook and open it. Identify the value of
**`workflow_start`** - the id of the single `start` step.

```sh
cp ~/cacao/template_block_ip.json ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
nano ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the id referenced by `workflow_start`.
levels.solution:
1. `cp ~/cacao/template_block_ip.json ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. `grep workflow_start ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
3. Submit **`start--01`**.

hints.title: What links the workflow?
hints.content: `workflow_start` names the entry step; each step chains to the next via `on_completion`.

levels.title: 14. The block verb (UML 4-5)
levels.content:
Look at the `action--block-ip` step in your playbook. Identify the **nftables
verb** that discards the malicious packets.

**Answer:** the single nftables keyword.
levels.solution:
1. `grep -A12 action--block-ip ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. The command ends with `... counter drop`.
3. Submit **`drop`**.

hints.title: Discard vs reject
hints.content: One verb silently discards packets (no reply); that is the one used here.

levels.title: 15. Give your playbook a valid id (UML 4)
levels.content:
The template id `playbook--REPLACE-WITH-UUID` is only a placeholder. A CACAO id
is `playbook--<uuid-v4>` and it is also the key under which NG-SOAR (KMS) stores
your playbook. Generate a UUID and set it now, **before** creating the playbook
in NG-SOAR.

```sh
uuidgen
# edit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json -> "id": "playbook--<that-uuid>"
```

While editing, also set `playbook_variables.source_ip.value` to the malicious IP
from the brief.

**Answer:** the mandatory prefix of a CACAO playbook id.
levels.solution:
1. `uuidgen` -> e.g. `3b1d2f0a-9b2e-4d1c-8a77-0a1b2c3d4e5f`.
2. Set `"id": "playbook--3b1d2f0a-..."` and `source_ip.value` = `10.10.10.10`.
3. The mandatory prefix is **`playbook--`**.

hints.title: Format expected
hints.content: See `schema_hints.md`: the id is `playbook--<uuid-v4>`.

levels.title: 16. Create the playbook in NG-SOAR (UML 4)
levels.content:
Create your playbook **in NG-SOAR**: it is stored in the KMS under its CACAO id,
not yet validated.

```sh
cacao-client create ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the KMS `status` returned for your newly created playbook.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client create ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. NG-SOAR replies `{"kms_id": "playbook--...", "status": "draft"}`.
3. Submit **`draft`**.

hints.title: Error about the id?
hints.content: NG-SOAR refuses to store a playbook whose `id` is not `playbook--<uuid-v4>`. Fix it (previous level) and retry.

levels.title: 17. CACAO structure check

questions.text: How many 'start' steps must a valid CACAO workflow contain?
Which participant provides the templates, schema hints and supported firewall commands (UML 5)?
Match each CACAO step type to its role.

extended_matching_options.text: Runs a command (e.g. the host firewall block)

levels.instructions: Verify your understanding of CACAO structure and of who provides what.

levels.title: 18. Phase 3 - Validation (UML 6-10)
levels.content:
# Validation loop

- **UML 6** - you **submit** the playbook for validation;
- **UML 7** - NG-SOAR validates **CACAO syntax, workflow logic and required
  parameters**;
- **UML 8** - NG-SOAR returns the result: **errors** or **approval**;
- **UML 9** - if it fails, you **correct and resubmit**;
- **UML 10** - once approved, NG-SOAR notifies the **NG-SOAR Operator** that the
  playbook is **ready for execution** (it is queued for the operator; you cannot
  execute it yourself).

```sh
cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```
The response contains `approved`, `errors`, `warnings`, `attempt` and the new
KMS `status`.

You will *deliberately* trigger two validation errors to learn how NG-SOAR
reports them, then reach a clean approval.

levels.title: 19. Trigger a syntax error (UML 6-8)
levels.content:
Temporarily remove the `workflow_start` line from `~/cacao/my_playbook.json` and
submit it.

```sh
cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the field named in the `missing required field` error.
(Restore the line afterwards.)
levels.solution:
1. Delete `"workflow_start": "start--01",` and save.
2. `cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
3. `errors` contains `missing required field: 'workflow_start'`.
4. Submit **`workflow_start`** and restore the line.

hints.title: Where is the verdict?
hints.content: The `errors` array lists each problem; read the missing-field message.

levels.title: 20. Trigger a workflow-logic error (UML 7-9)
levels.content:
Temporarily point the start step's `on_completion` to a non-existent step
(e.g. `action--nope`) and resubmit.

**Answer:** the step field named in the `unknown step` error.
(Restore `action--block-ip` afterwards.)
levels.solution:
1. Set `start--01.on_completion` to `action--nope`, save.
2. `cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
3. Error: `step 'start--01': on_completion -> unknown step 'action--nope'`.
4. Submit **`on_completion`** and restore the value.

hints.title: Which field chains steps?
hints.content: The one naming the next step to run after the current one.

levels.title: 21. Get your playbook approved (UML 8-9)
levels.content:
Fix everything (valid `id`, `workflow_start`, `on_completion` links, `source_ip`
= `10.10.10.10`, the `input` drop command) and resubmit until it passes.

```sh
cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the value of `approved` once it passes.
levels.solution:
1. Compare with `~/cacao/sample_block_ip_playbook.json` if needed.
2. `cacao-client submit ~/cacao/my_playbook.json` returns `"approved": true`
   and an empty `errors` array.
3. Submit **`true`**.

hints.title: Still failing?
hints.content: Fix the entries in `errors` one by one; compare against `~/cacao/sample_block_ip_playbook.json`.

levels.title: 22. Ready for execution (UML 10)
levels.content:
After approval NG-SOAR hands the playbook to the **NG-SOAR Operator** queue.
Check the KMS status of your playbook.

```sh
cacao-client status ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the KMS `status` of your approved playbook.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client status ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. Status moved `draft` -> `ready-for-execution`.
3. Submit **`ready-for-execution`**.

hints.title: Status is 'rejected'?
hints.content: Your last submission failed validation. Resubmit a corrected version (level 21).

levels.title: 23. Validation knowledge check

questions.text: Match each NG-SOAR validation error to its root cause.

extended_matching_options.text: The playbook has no action step whose command drops/blocks traffic
workflow_start points to a step id that is not defined
The id is not 'playbook--' followed by a UUID v4
No source_ip playbook variable and no __SOURCE_IP__ placeholder

extended_matching_statements.text: 'workflow_start' does not reference an existing step

questions.text: Who is notified that an approved playbook is ready for execution (UML 10)?

levels.instructions: Match each validator message to what causes it.

levels.title: 24. Phase 4 - Execution (UML 11-14)
levels.content:
# Execution

- **UML 11** - the **NG-SOAR Operator** executes the validated playbook;
- **UML 12** - NG-SOAR applies the **host firewall rule** on the Lab Target Service
  (drop the malicious source IP in the nftables `input` chain);
- **UML 13** - NG-SOAR **verifies the block** by probing the target **from the
  malicious IP** (the attacker) - the probe must return `BLOCKED`;
- **UML 14** - NG-SOAR provides **you** the execution logs, status and host
  firewall evidence.

Separation of duties: the Student authors, the NG-SOAR Operator executes. You
will first confirm that you *cannot* execute, then switch to the operator role.

### NG-SOAR Operator role card
| | |
|---|---|
| Host | `ng-soar` (10.10.30.10) |
| User | `soar-operator` |
| Password | `Operator2d!` |
| Commands | `soar-operator queue`, `soar-operator execute <playbook-id>` |

levels.title: 25. Baseline - the service is reachable (UML 11)
levels.content:
Before the block, confirm the Lab Target Service is up (its host firewall
`input` chain has a default `accept` policy).

```sh
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://10.10.20.10/
```

**Answer:** the HTTP status code returned.
levels.solution:
1. Run the curl one-liner.
2. The service answers **`200`**. (Only the malicious IP will be blocked, so
   your console keeps getting 200 after the block too.)

hints.title: What status means OK?
hints.content: The canonical HTTP success code is a three-digit number starting with 2.

levels.title: 26. Students cannot execute (UML 11)
levels.content:
Try to execute your approved playbook from the Student console.

```sh
cacao-client execute ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

**Answer:** the HTTP status code NG-SOAR returns.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client execute ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. NG-SOAR answers `HTTP 403` - `forbidden: execution is reserved to the NG-SOAR Operator`.
3. Submit **`403`**.

hints.title: Which code means forbidden?
hints.content: Authenticated but not allowed: a 4xx code between 401 and 404.

levels.title: 27. NG-SOAR Operator: review the queue (UML 10-11)
levels.content:
Switch hats: log in to NG-SOAR as the **NG-SOAR Operator** (role card in level
24) and list the playbooks that are ready for execution.

```sh
ssh soar-operator@10.10.30.10
soar-operator queue
```

**Answer:** the `source_ip` the queued playbook will block.
levels.solution:
1. `ssh soar-operator@10.10.30.10` (password `Operator2d!`).
2. `soar-operator queue` lists your playbook id, name, `ready-for-execution` and
   `source_ip 10.10.10.10`.
3. Submit **`10.10.10.10`**.

hints.title: Queue is empty?
hints.content: Only approved playbooks are queued. Make sure `cacao-client status` shows `ready-for-execution` for yours.

levels.title: 28. NG-SOAR Operator: execute the playbook (UML 11-13)
levels.content:
Still as the NG-SOAR Operator, execute the approved playbook. NG-SOAR applies
the host firewall rule on `lab-target` (UML 12) and verifies the block from the
malicious IP (UML 13).

```sh
soar-operator execute <playbook-id>     # the id shown by 'soar-operator queue'
```

**Answer:** the execution `status` on a fully successful run.
levels.solution:
1. `soar-operator execute playbook--<your-uuid>`.
2. The result is **`success`** (rule applied and probe BLOCKED).
3. Log out (`exit`) to return to the Student console.

hints.title: Got 'completed-with-warnings'?
hints.content: The block did not verify. Check that `source_ip` is `10.10.10.10`, resubmit, and execute again.

levels.title: 29. Retrieve the host firewall evidence (UML 12, 14)
levels.content:
Back on the Student console, fetch the execution report NG-SOAR provides you:
logs, status and **host firewall evidence** (the `lab-target` nftables ruleset).

```sh
cacao-client report ~/cacao/my_playbook.json
```

The executor tags the rule it added with a **comment**.

**Answer:** the exact rule comment.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client report ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. In `firewall_evidence` the `input` chain shows
   `ip saddr 10.10.10.10 counter packets N bytes M drop comment "cacao-block-10.10.10.10"`.
3. Submit **`cacao-block-10.10.10.10`**.

hints.title: Where is the comment?
hints.content: At the end of the drop rule line in `firewall_evidence`: `comment "..."`.

levels.title: 30. Verify the block from the malicious IP (UML 13)
levels.content:
In the same report read `verification.probe_output`: the result of NG-SOAR
driving a probe **from the attacker (malicious IP)** to the Lab Target Service
after the rule was applied.

**Answer:** the token the probe prints when the connection is dropped.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client report ~/cacao/my_playbook.json`.
2. `verification.blocked` is `true` and `probe_output` is **`BLOCKED`**.

hints.title: What does the probe do?
hints.content: It curls the target from the attacker; on failure it prints one upper-case word.

levels.title: 31. Execution knowledge check

questions.text: What proves that the malicious source IP is actually blocked?

choices.text: The probe from the malicious IP can no longer reach the target, and the drop rule counter increases
The playbook has an end step

questions.text: In which nftables chain of the Lab Target Service was the drop rule added?

levels.instructions: A short test on the execution phase.

levels.title: 32. Phase 5 - Feedback (UML 15-16)
levels.content:
# Feedback

- **UML 15** - the **Cyber Range** compiles your **playbook**, the **validation
  results** and the **execution logs** and sends them to **Evaluation/Reporting**.
  This is done automatically by the platform (`cr-compile`, every 30 s); you can
  trigger it immediately with `cr-compile --now`.
- **UML 16** - **Evaluation/Reporting** returns your **training summary**.

```sh
cr-compile --now
cacao-client summary
```

levels.title: 33. Cyber Range compilation (UML 15)
levels.content:
Trigger the compilation and read the `compiled_artifacts` list in the summary.

```sh
cr-compile --now
cacao-client summary
```

**Answer:** how many artifacts the Cyber Range compiled for Evaluation/Reporting.
levels.solution:
1. `cr-compile --now`, then `cacao-client summary`.
2. `compiled_artifacts` = `["student_playbook", "validation_results", "execution_logs"]`.
3. Submit **`3`**.

hints.title: Look at the UML
hints.content: Step 15 lists what is compiled: the student playbook, the validation results and the execution logs.

levels.title: 34. Training summary (UML 16)
levels.content:
Read your **grade** in the training summary returned by Evaluation/Reporting.

```sh
cacao-client summary
```

**Answer:** the value of `grade`.
levels.solution:
1. `cacao-client summary`.
2. It shows `validation_attempts`, `validation_approved`, `executed_by`
   (`ng-soar-operator`), `traffic_blocked`, `execution_status` and `grade`.
3. With an approved playbook and blocked traffic the grade is **`PASS`**.

hints.title: Grade shows REVIEW?
hints.content: Validation was not approved or traffic was not blocked. Redo levels 21 and 28, run `cr-compile --now` and fetch the summary again.

levels.title: 35. Training feedback

questions.text: What did you find most valuable in this CACAO playbook authoring training?
Which step or concept (CACAO structure, validation, operator execution, nftables) was hardest, and why?
What recommendations do you have for future enhancements of this scenario?

levels.instructions: Help us improve this training. Your answers are anonymous and are not graded.
